title: A green that reached one file
scenario:
A bakery chain changes its brand green. Lena, the design lead, owns the token file and the Figma library. The app team works in Figma, the kids' menu team in Penpot, and the developers use Claude Code. Four things went wrong this week. You read the log.

Use the exhibit. The bakery, the people and the log are made up for this case. Tool details are from the vendors' pages in October 2026.
exhibit:
WEEK LOG (made up)

  1. Mon  Lena changes color/brand in the "Core" library file
          in Figma: #21734d -> #1b5e3f.
     Tue  The app team's Figma files still show #21734d.
          Lena's Libraries icon shows a blue badge.

  2. Tue  A Claude Code agent, asked to "fix low contrast",
          edits tokens/brand.tokens.json itself.
          CLAUDE.md already says: "Never edit tokens/".
          Lena wants this blocked, not just asked.

  3. Wed  A developer wants to delete color.mint today.
          It is still used on 30 screens.

  4. Thu  In Penpot, Sam clicks Import tokens on the connected
          Core library. The kids' file had its own Dark theme.
          After the import, that theme is gone. No export
          was made first.

questions.prompt: Log 1: why do the app team's files still show the old green?

options.text: Figma copies library changes to other files once a week
options.explanation: No page here says that. Changes stay in the library file until they are published.

options.text: The change is not published; publish it, then teams accept
options.explanation: Right. The Figma docs say changes only appear in the current file until you publish them. Others then review and accept.

options.text: The variable is hidden when publishing, so it never left
options.explanation: Lena's blue badge means the change still needs to be published. Nothing in the log says the variable was hidden.

options.text: Each app designer must type the new hex in by hand
options.explanation: That makes many copies of one colour. Publish the library once and let teams accept the update.

questions.prompt: Log 2: Lena wants the agent blocked from the token files. What does that?

options.text: A second CLAUDE.md inside tokens/ that repeats the rule
options.explanation: That is still a rule file. Chapter 3: a rule guides; it does not lock.

options.text: Telling the agent in chat, at the start of every session
options.explanation: A chat line is guidance too, and it is easy to forget. It blocks nothing.

options.text: Renaming the folder so that the agent cannot find it
options.explanation: The agent can still list and open files. A deny rule is the lock the Claude Code docs name.

options.text: An Edit deny rule for tokens/, checked into version control
options.explanation: Right. The Claude Code docs say to add an Edit deny rule for paths no tool may change, and settings can be shared in version control.

questions.prompt: Log 3: color.mint is still used on 30 screens. What should happen first?

options.text: Mark it $deprecated with what to use instead; delete it later
options.explanation: Right. The spec's $deprecated marks a token to stop using, and it lists that removing it now may break existing support.

options.text: Delete it today, since tools will guess a near colour for it
options.explanation: The spec lists that removing a token now may break existing support. Thirty screens still use it.

options.text: Rename it to color.old-mint so nobody picks it by accident
options.explanation: A new name drops the old one, so the 30 screens lose it just as with a delete (our reading).

options.text: Keep it as is and tell people in chat to stop using it
options.explanation: A chat note is easy to miss. $deprecated puts the note on the token itself.

questions.prompt: Log 4: the kids' Dark theme is gone after Import tokens. Why?

options.text: Penpot merges tokens, so the Dark theme was never saved
options.explanation: Penpot does not merge here. It says import replaces all tokens, sets and themes.

options.text: Import replaces all tokens, sets and themes in the file
options.explanation: Right. The Penpot docs say importing from a library replaces them all, and to export tokens first to keep a backup.

options.text: Connecting the Core library deleted the file's own themes
options.explanation: Connecting a library shares its assets. The Penpot docs say token import is a separate step.

options.text: Dark themes cannot live in a file that uses a library
options.explanation: No page says that. The import replaced the file's tokens, sets and themes.
